For a buyer the practical points are the form bought, the basis a result is reported on, where the bread came from and the laboratory’s reporting limit. Testing finds contamination but does not remove it.

<div class="hmi-analyte-explorer" id="hmi-occurrence-bread" data-analyte-explorer data-compact-intro="true" data-source-summaries="true"><details class="hmi-drawer-disclosure" data-explorer-context><summary data-open-context aria-haspopup="dialog" aria-controls="hmi-occurrence-bread-drawer">Comparison methods and scope</summary><div data-explorer-context-content>

<p>Each row is one statistic a source reports for one form of bread, group and metal; percentiles, ranges and maxima reported for the same samples as a mean or median are shown on that row. Different forms and preparation states are kept apart, and dry-weight results never share a reference with as-sold or fresh-weight results. Ratings place a result against an HMI reference built from monitoring results and ordinary-setting medians for the same form and basis. Same-study contrasts compare a contaminated or treated site with its control, targeted with random sampling, a prepared form with the unprocessed one, or one group of a study with the median of its other groups. Held rows failed a check against their own source and are shown but not compared.</p>

At least four reference units and a definitely positive Q1 to Q3 spread are required. This is a display eligibility rule, not statistical validation.</p><p class="hmi-drawer-section-title" role="heading" aria-level="3">Limitations</p><p>2 sampling families with different designs; none is a probability sample of world supply. Reporting regions and purchase markets are not growing areas. Non-detects with differing limits widen the bounds. <a id="sources-and-contamination-pathways"></a>
## How metals reach bread

<a id="hmi-ing-010"></a>
<a id="what-evidence-supports-root-uptake-surface-deposition-feed-transfer-or-other-biological-pathways"></a>
<a id="hmi-ing-011"></a>
<a id="what-contamination-can-arise-from-agricultural-inputs-harvesting-processing-equipment-or-packaging"></a>
<a id="hmi-ing-012"></a>
<a id="which-source-attribution-claims-are-measured-modelled-inferred-or-unresolved"></a>

The evidence on how metals reach bread comes from studies that compared exposed and ordinary settings. Bread, as sold from Barbari, traditional oven, after baking had Co higher at 50 µg/kg, against 25 µg/kg for all bread types, industrial oven in the same study.<sup class="cite">[[sources/ghasemi2022-mashhad-bread-baking-methods-metals|8]]<span class="cite-card"><span class="cite-card-head"><span class="cite-card-authors">Ghasemi S, Hashemi M, Gholian Aval M, Safarian M, Khanzadi S, Orooji A, Tavakoly Sany SB · 2022</span><a class="cite-card-title" href="../sources/ghasemi2022-mashhad-bread-baking-methods-metals">Effect of Baking Methods Types on Residues of Heavy Metals in the Different Breads Produced with Wheat Flour in Iran: A Case Study of Mashhad</a></span><span class="cite-card-body"><span class="cite-card-journal">Journal of Chemical Health Risks 12(1), 105-113</span><a class="cite-card-review" href="../sources/ghasemi2022-mashhad-bread-baking-methods-metals">Read source →</a></span></span></sup> In another study, bread, as sold from bread from bakeries using coal ovens, Jalingo had Fe higher at 757 µg/kg, against 423 µg/kg for bread from bakeries using electric ovens, Jalingo in the same study.<sup class="cite">[[sources/tutuwa2023-jalingo-bread-baking-fuel-metals|7]]<span class="cite-card"><span class="cite-card-head"><span class="cite-card-authors">Tutuwa JA, Bando CD, Tadawus RH, Ifraimu D, Aigbogun BS, Nuhu I, Jesse PS, Agbu TD · 2023</span><a class="cite-card-title" href="../sources/tutuwa2023-jalingo-bread-baking-fuel-metals">Assessement of the Influence of Baking Fuel Types on the Residues of Some Heavy Metals in Selected Bread from Jalingo, Taraba State</a></span><span class="cite-card-body"><span class="cite-card-journal">Journal of Multidisciplinary Sciences: MIKAILALSYS 2(1): 25-31</span><a class="cite-card-review" href="../sources/tutuwa2023-jalingo-bread-baking-fuel-metals">Read source →</a></span></span></sup>

These are observational comparisons from single studies; the size of the difference depends on the site, metal and distance.



<a id="ranges-by-source-region-and-variety"></a>
## Which forms and regions measured lower

<a id="hmi-ing-013"></a>
<a id="how-do-concentrations-vary-by-origin-growing-conditions-variety-and-harvest-period"></a>
<a id="hmi-ing-014"></a>
<a id="what-evidence-distinguishes-within-lot-between-lot-supplier-and-production-system-variation"></a>
<a id="hmi-ing-015"></a>
<a id="which-comparisons-support-a-sourcing-decision-and-where-would-geographic-or-supplier-generalization-be-unjustified"></a>

For cadmium, the HMI reference median was lowest for bread, cooked (17.1 µg/kg) and highest for bread, as sold (19.3 µg/kg); forms differ in water content, so this compares foods as sold or eaten, not Avoiding exposed growing areas lowered the metal measured in the studies available, but no study measured the cost or supply effect of doing so.<sup class="cite">[[sources/ghasemi2022-mashhad-bread-baking-methods-metals|8]]<span class="cite-card"><span class="cite-card-head"><span class="cite-card-authors">Ghasemi S, Hashemi M, Gholian Aval M, Safarian M, Khanzadi S, Orooji A, Tavakoly Sany SB · 2022</span><a class="cite-card-title" href="../sources/ghasemi2022-mashhad-bread-baking-methods-metals">Effect of Baking Methods Types on Residues of Heavy Metals in the Different Breads Produced with Wheat Flour in Iran: A Case Study of Mashhad</a></span><span class="cite-card-body"><span class="cite-card-journal">Journal of Chemical Health Risks 12(1), 105-113</span><a class="cite-card-review" href="../sources/ghasemi2022-mashhad-bread-baking-methods-metals">Read source →</a></span></span></sup> Metals do not move together, so a lot that passes a lead limit says little about cadmium, arsenic or nickel unless those are tested as well.

Reporting limits for lead ranged from 2 µg/kg (WHO GEMS/Food) to 80 µg/kg (Gacal et al. 2023), so a non-detect from a less sensitive method says much less.<sup class="cite">[[sources/who-gemsfood-heavy-metal-contaminants|1]]<span class="cite-card"><span class="cite-card-head"><span class="cite-card-authors">World Health Organization · 2026</span><a class="cite-card-title" href="../sources/who-gemsfood-heavy-metal-contaminants">GEMS/Food Contaminants database heavy-metal exports</a></span><span class="cite-card-body"><span class="cite-card-journal">GEMS/Food Contamination Monitoring and Assessment Programme</span><a class="cite-card-review" href="../sources/who-gemsfood-heavy-metal-contaminants">Read source →</a></span></span></sup><sup class="cite">[[sources/gacal2023-cadmium-lead-bread-gluten-free-poland|15]]<span class="cite-card"><span class="cite-card-head"><span class="cite-card-authors">Gacal M, Gut-Pietrasz K, Cwielag-Drabek M · 2023</span><a class="cite-card-title" href="../sources/gacal2023-cadmium-lead-bread-gluten-free-poland">Cadmium and lead content in gluten and gluten-free bread available on Polish market - <summary><span class="mk" aria-hidden="true"></span>How do heavy metals get into bread?</summary>
<div class="ans" data-hmi-faq-answer="1">

In the studies available, bread from contaminated or exposed settings carried more metal than bread from the same study’s control.<sup class="cite">[[sources/tutuwa2023-jalingo-bread-baking-fuel-metals|7]]<span class="cite-card"><span class="cite-card-head"><span class="cite-card-authors">Tutuwa JA, Bando CD, Tadawus RH, Ifraimu D, Aigbogun BS, Nuhu I, Jesse PS, Agbu TD · 2023</span><a class="cite-card-title" href="../sources/tutuwa2023-jalingo-bread-baking-fuel-metals">Assessement of the Influence of Baking Fuel Types on the Residues of Some Heavy Metals in Selected Bread from Jalingo, Taraba State</a></span><span class="cite-card-body"><span class="cite-card-journal">Journal of Multidisciplinary Sciences: MIKAILALSYS 2(1): 25-31</span><a class="cite-card-review" href="../sources/tutuwa2023-jalingo-bread-baking-fuel-metals">Read source →</a></span></span></sup> Bread, as sold from bread from bakeries using coal ovens, Jalingo had lead higher at 296 µg/kg, against 181 µg/kg for bread from bakeries using electric ovens, Jalingo in the same study.<sup class="cite">[[sources/tutuwa2023-jalingo-bread-baking-fuel-metals|7]]<span class="cite-card"><span class="cite-card-head"><span class="cite-card-authors">Tutuwa JA, Bando CD, Tadawus RH, Ifraimu D, Aigbogun BS, Nuhu I, Jesse PS, Agbu TD · 2023</span><a class="cite-card-title" href="../sources/tutuwa2023-jalingo-bread-baking-fuel-metals">Assessement of the Influence of Baking Fuel Types on the Residues of Some Heavy Metals in Selected Bread from Jalingo, Taraba State</a></span><span class="cite-card-body"><span class="cite-card-journal">Journal of Multidisciplinary Sciences: MIKAILALSYS 2(1): 25-31</span><a class="cite-card-review" href="../sources/tutuwa2023-jalingo-bread-baking-fuel-metals">Read source →</a></span></span></sup>

</div>
</details>

<details class="qa" data-hmi-faq="1" id="which-types-of-bread-have-the-lowest-levels" data-anchor="which-types-of-bread-have-the-lowest-levels" data-question="Which types of bread have the lowest levels?">
<summary><span class="mk" aria-hidden="true"></span>Which types of bread have the lowest levels?</summary>
<div class="ans" data-hmi-faq-answer="1">

For cadmium, the HMI reference median was lowest for bread, cooked (17.1 µg/kg) and highest for bread, as sold (19.3 µg/kg); forms differ in water content, so this compares foods as sold or eaten, not uptake.<sup class="cite">[[sources/who-gemsfood-heavy-metal-contaminants|1]]<span class="cite-card"><span class="cite-card-head"><span class="cite-card-authors">World Health Organization · 2026</span><a class="cite-card-title" href="../sources/who-gemsfood-heavy-metal-contaminants">GEMS/Food Contaminants database heavy-metal exports</a></span><span class="cite-card-body"><span class="cite-card-journal">GEMS/Food Contamination Monitoring and Assessment Programme</span><a class="cite-card-review" href="../sources/who-gemsfood-heavy-metal-contaminants">Read source →</a></span></span></sup><sup class="cite">[[sources/authors2025-evaluation-of-concentrations-and-health-risk-assessment-of|2]]<span class="cite-card"><span class="cite-card-head"><span class="cite-card-authors">Unknown authors · 2025</span><a class="cite-card-title" href="../sources/authors2025-evaluation-of-concentrations-and-health-risk-assessment-of">Evaluation of Concentrations and Health Risk Assessment of Cadmium, Lead, Chromium and Arsenic in</a></span><span class="cite-card-body"><span class="cite-card-journal">Peer-reviewed article</span><a class="cite-card-review" href="../sources/authors2025-evaluation-of-concentrations-and-health-risk-assessment-of">Read source →</a></span></span></sup>

</div>
</details>

<details class="qa" data-hmi-faq="1" id="which-regions-report-the-lowest-levels-in-bread" data-anchor="which-regions-report-the-lowest-levels-in-bread" data-question="Which regions report the lowest levels in bread?">
<summary><span class="mk" aria-hidden="true"></span>Which regions report the lowest levels in bread?</summary>
<div class="ans" data-hmi-faq-answer="1">

Among GEMS/Food reporting regions, bread, as sold had the lowest cadmium subgroup median in WPRO (14 µg/kg) and the highest in EURO (16.5 µg/kg); reporting regions are markets, not growing areas.<sup class="cite">[[sources/who-gemsfood-heavy-metal-contaminants|1]]<span class="cite-card"><span class="cite-card-head"><span class="cite-card-authors">World Health Organization · 2026</span><a class="cite-card-title" href="../sources/who-gemsfood-heavy-metal-contaminants">GEMS/Food Contaminants database heavy-metal exports</a></span><span class="cite-card-body"><span class="cite-card-journal">GEMS/Food Contamination Monitoring and Assessment Programme</span><a class="cite-card-review" href="../sources/who-gemsfood-heavy-metal-contaminants">Read source →</a></span></span></sup> For total arsenic, the lowest regional median was in WPRO (8.17 µg/kg) and the highest in EURO (225 µg/kg).<sup class="cite">[[sources/who-gemsfood-heavy-metal-contaminants|1]]<span class="cite-card"><span class="cite-card-head"><span class="cite-card-authors">World Health Organization · 2026</span><a class="cite-card-title" href="../sources/who-gemsfood-heavy-metal-contaminants">GEMS/Food Contaminants database heavy-metal exports</a></span><span class="cite-card-body"><span class="cite-card-journal">GEMS/Food Contamination Monitoring and Assessment Programme</span><a class="cite-card-review" href="../sources/who-gemsfood-heavy-metal-contaminants">Read source →</a></span></span></sup>

</div>
</details>

<details class="qa" data-hmi-faq="1" id="does-processing-change-heavy-metals-in-bread" data-anchor="does-processing-change-heavy-metals-in-bread" data-question="Does processing change heavy metals in bread?">
<summary><span class="mk" aria-hidden="true"></span>Does processing change heavy metals in bread?</summary>
<div class="ans" data-hmi-faq-answer="1">

Only comparisons between forms in the same study are available, not before-and-after measurements of the same bread.<sup class="cite">[[sources/cfs2013-hktds-metallic-contaminants|13]]<span class="cite-card"><span class="cite-card-head"><span class="cite-card-authors">Centre for Food Safety (Hong Kong) · 2013</span><a class="cite-card-title" href="../sources/cfs2013-hktds-metallic-contaminants">The First Hong Kong Total Diet Study: Metallic Contaminants</a></span><span class="cite-card-body"><span class="cite-card-journal">Centre for Food Safety, Food and Environmental Hygiene Department, Government of the Hong Kong Special Administrative Region</span><a class="cite-card-review" href="../sources/cfs2013-hktds-metallic-contaminants">Read source →</a></span></span></sup> Bread, cooked (all samples) had lead lower at 6 µg/kg, against 7 µg/kg for the unprocessed form in the same group (bread, as sold).<sup class="cite">[[sources/cfs2013-hktds-metallic-contaminants|13]]<span class="cite-card"><span class="cite-card-head"><span class="cite-card-authors">Centre for Food Safety (Hong Kong) · 2013</span><a class="cite-card-title" href="../sources/cfs2013-hktds-metallic-contaminants">The First Hong Kong Total Diet Study: Metallic Contaminants</a></span><span class="cite-card-body"><span class="cite-card-journal">Centre for Food Safety, Food and Environmental Hygiene Department, Government of the Hong Kong Special Administrative Region</span><a class="cite-card-review" href="../sources/cfs2013-hktds-metallic-contaminants">Read source →</a></span></span></sup>

</div>
</details>

<details class="qa" data-hmi-faq="1" id="how-much-of-the-arsenic-in-bread-is-inorganic" data-anchor="how-much-of-the-arsenic-in-bread-is-inorganic" data-question="How much of the arsenic in bread is inorganic?">
<summary><span class="mk" aria-hidden="true"></span>How much of the arsenic in bread is inorganic?</summary>
<div class="ans" data-hmi-faq-answer="1">
